chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, narrated it from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

It was said to him that a man married a young girl, so his wife breast-fed her, and then another wife of his breast-fed her. Ibn Shubrumah said: 'The girl and both his wives are prohibited to him.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Ibn Shubrumah erred. The girl is prohibited to him, and the wife who breast-fed her first. As for the last one, she is not prohibited to him, as if she had breast-fed her own daughter.'
ai.seo_question: How many breast-feedings create a marital prohibition in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that milk kinship (radāʿ) is established primarily through the first nursing event, distinguishing it from the view of the judge Ibn Shubrumah who extended the prohibition to both wives. It underscores the significance of chronological precedence in determining mahram relationships, a key nuance in Shia fiqh that impacts marriage validity and inheritance rights.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, reporting it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘It was said to him<sup>asws</sup> that a man married a young girl, so his wife breast-fed her, and another wife of his breast-fed her. So Ibn Shubrama (a judge) said that the girl and both his wife are Prohibited unto him’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ibn Shubrama has erred. The girl is Prohibited unto him and the wife who breast-fed her first. So, as for the last one, so she is not Prohibited unto him, as if she had breast-fed her own daughter’.
en.sarwar: 12. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who allows her milk without giving birth and breastfeeds a girl or a boy with that milk; if because of such milk the unlawfulness on account of breastfeeding comes into existence. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, unlawfulness does not come into existence.’”
